name: Guake
summary: Drop-down (quake-style) terminal for GNOME and other GTK desktops (Python, GTK3, VTE) with tabs, splits, transparency, background image and a global show/hide hotkey. Settings live in dconf, not in a file.
configFormat: dconf/gsettings (schemas guake.*, path /org/guake/), no config file

install.notes: Debian/Ubuntu (sudo apt install guake); the docs also list a PPA, ppa:linuxuprising/guake, for newer releases.
PyPI route (pipx install guake); needs the GTK/VTE/keybinder system packages listed in the docs. Prefer the distro package.

linux.notes: No config file: all settings are dconf keys in schemas guake, guake.general, guake.style, guake.style.font, guake.style.background, guake.keybindings.* (installed system-wide with the package, so plain gsettings works). Back up first with `dconf dump /org/guake/ > backup.ini` (restore: `dconf load /org/guake/ < backup.ini`). Requires a running dconf/D-Bus session of the desktop user. On Wayland the built-in global hotkey (keybinder) does not work: the docs say to add a GNOME custom keyboard shortcut running `guake-toggle` instead. Start it with `guake` (autostart: set guake.general start-at-login true). Whether running instances pick up every key change live is unverified; restart Guake if a change does not show.
